The Integration Pitch

Every New Health-System Partner Is Another EHR to Plumb Before HealthVision Can Predict Anything

HDAI's entire value proposition depends on getting clean, current clinical data out of someone else's EHR fast — and every new logo, from a community hospital to an academic cancer center like Dana-Farber, arrives on a different Epic, Oracle Health, or athenahealth instance with its own quirks. Today that ingestion work competes for the same engineering hours that should be spent improving HealthVision's risk models and generative summarization.

The highest-leverage moment is now: HDAI is mid-scale-up on a $31M Series C, has just proven its LLM chart-summarization approach at Dana-Farber, and is deep in a system-wide rollout at Houston Methodist. A repeatable, standards-based interoperability layer turns each new health-system go-live from a bespoke integration project into a configuration exercise — shortening time-to-first-prediction for every future HealthVision deployment.

Vorro's platform gives HDAI's engineering and clinical teams a single FHIR/HL7/C-CDA pipe to Epic, Oracle Health, and athenahealth instances, plus the claims and payer feeds value-based partners bring — so Dr. Cullen's clinical roadmap, not integration backlog, sets the pace of HealthVision's next expansion.
